vulnerability.name: Apache Tomcat AJP Ghostcat File Read (CVE-2020-1938)
vulnerability.author: Thomas Shaw
vulnerability.description:
Apache Tomcat's AJP connector is exposed on all interfaces (0.0.0.0:8009) with no shared secret and arbitrary request attributes allowed, which is the "Ghostcat" misconfiguration behind CVE-2020-1938. An unauthenticated attacker speaking AJP can set the javax.servlet.include.* request attributes to make Tomcat read any file under the web application, including files under WEB-INF that are never served over HTTP.
Version-vs-CVE note: the service module installs Tomcat 9.0.123, which ships the 9.0.31 fix (AJP bound to localhost, secretRequired=true, request attributes blocked by default). This module deliberately restores the pre-9.0.31 behaviour on the connector - address="0.0.0.0", secretRequired="false" and allowedRequestAttributesPattern=".*" - which is a documented real-world misconfiguration that re-opens the exact Ghostcat file read. The stock Metasploit auxiliary reads the planted WEB-INF file against this configuration unchanged.
